Trailesque
They don't make langorous, emotional, fractured family dramas like this any more, do they? Imho it is a bit overrated, probably due to the starpower involved. A man named Travis stumbles mutely out of the desert, his brother comes and takes him back to his place, and here the story grows complicated. There is a boy there, the lost fellow's son, and he is really at the heart of the story. Images of the big, lonesome American West play a key role too. (SPOILER ALERT) Despite the fact that the kid is being well taken care of by his aunt and uncle, his absentee dad takes him on the road for Texas, and a hoped-for encounter with the woman (beautiful Kinski) who left them both behind. A lot of it is slow and none too thrilling, but there is a powerful emotional climax waiting (Shepard was good at writing those) if you stick it out. The title btw refers to the place where Travis wants to build a happy home - something that he - and we - know ain't gonna happen.

Creo que me ganaré mucho detractores, pero esta cinta está legísima de ser la gran obra maestra que muchos creen; está muy muy lejos, tal vez como Texas del mismo Paris. Tratare de dar a entender el porque; que una película tenga planos antiguos, y música instrumental ambiental y sea una road movie no la hace buena, la hace tal vez estéticamente rica pero su esencia carece de muchas ideas, trata a ser profunda pero es muy pretenciosa. No explica el porqué de las relaciones tormentosas en las 2 horas de duración, ni quienes son los personajes, solo sus caras tristes y epifanías que aportan poco, me pareció más un metraje experimental, y si es bueno como eso, pero no es la gran obra del séptimo arte, puede ser un referente pero en mi caso es un referente muy lejano. Destacable la última escena, tal vez difícil de hacer para su época pero para mi no ha envejecido bien, se ha quedado como una obra corta y poco innovadora, tal vez su actriz sea muy guapa pero es que la idea no es ver una pasarela de moda. No es para mi. Creo entender por qué le gusta a la gente y es por eso mismo que no conecta, lo pretencioso sin argumentación definitivamente no es para **** fotografía es bonita, pero su contenido es como un desierto, lleno de arena y color marrón pálido, sin gracia.

Paris, Texas is a beautifully shot film with a unique atmosphere, but I had mixed feelings about it. While I appreciated the cinematography and the melancholic tone, I couldn’t quite connect with the lead actor’s performance. The film explores deep themes of loss and redemption, but at times, the slow pacing made it hard to stay engaged. The ending felt strange to me—not necessarily bad, but unexpected in a way that left me unsure how to feel about it. Still, the film has a certain charm that lingers.

arrivist
'Paris, Texas' is two-and-a-half hours long, but feels like four. It is undoubtedly very beautiful; the delicate texture of the celluloid, nearly every shot is carefully lit and composed, with some powerfully emotive scenes. The film is a slow meditation on self-realisation, and that reality is not every parent is fit to raise a child. Like all of Wenders' work, Paris Texas is unique, with moments of sheer beauty, yet at times, pretentious to the point of frustrating indifference.
